findings.actual_failure: Reproduced over a fixture store seeded with two defect captures whose statements share the first 60 slug chars: after the drain, docs/product/captured/ is empty — the first item carries terminal disposition routed while its materialized artifact was deleted by the second item's failed transaction, and the re-drain cannot recreate it because the capture is no longer open. That is exactly the state § D1 calls unrecoverable, and it contradicts transact_route's own docstring.
findings.observation: transact_route's rollback_partial_state unlinks the captured-item target whenever its bytes differ from the current item's expected bytes. _captured_item_target derives the filename from the statement slug truncated to 60 characters, so two captures whose statements share that prefix, or a pre-existing file at the same slug, collide: default_materialize raises FileExistsError, run_intake_transaction invokes the rollback, and the rollback deletes the differing pre-existing file — which can only be a complete artifact written by a prior committed transaction or by the normal capture path, never a partial write of this one.
findings.reachable_path: drain → transact_route → run_intake_transaction → materialize raises FileExistsError on the byte-differing existing target → _recover_partial_state → rollback_partial_state → target.unlink() of the other item's committed artifact.
findings.rule_ref: docs/specs/work-item-promotion-handoff/spec.md § D1 — the disposition-last ordering exists so no capture is ever closed without its handoff; AC-0005

findings.actual_failure: Reproduced over a fixture store holding one clean capture and one consistent dirty merged record: both read_open_captures and drain raise KnowledgeStoreError; the clean capture is never offered, no report is produced, and nothing is held. AC-0023's contracted outcome — held, with the refusing control named in the drain's report — cannot occur through the shipped drain entry point, and a single dirty merged record makes the drain unusable for every item in the store.
findings.observation: read_open_captures reads through knowledge_store._read_events, whose per-event validation re-runs the full capture-request validator including assert_persistable_text's eight patterns. A § D10 merge-path record whose free text carries a privacy-violating or instruction-shaped string therefore raises KnowledgeStoreError for the whole read before any offer is assembled. Because the store's read scan applies the same patterns over a superset of the fields rerun_prose_controls scans, a record that survives the reader can never fail the re-run: routing_input == refused is unreachable through drain(), and the § D4 re-run is dead code end-to-end.
findings.reachable_path: A record appended to the journal by direct file write (the merge path § D4 exists to handle), internally consistent (capture id and request digest recomputed over the dirty prose): read_open_captures and drain raise KnowledgeStoreError(privacy) for the entire store.
findings.rule_ref: docs/specs/work-item-promotion-handoff/spec.md § D4 / AC-0023 — a record failing a re-run prose control is refused as a routing input and held, with the refusing control named in the drain's report; § D11 / AC-0011 — an unattended drain reports the offers and holds every item

findings.actual_failure: Reproduced: parsing the drain's materialized files with the repository's own validator (work-loop _header_readiness.parse_captured_item) returns INVALID — field Kind for a routed question, field Detail for a routed defect — while existing captured-item files in docs/product/captured/ parse VALID. Every artifact the drain materializes is flagged invalid_captured_item by the repository's own close/reconciliation tooling, and for question routes the artifact produced is not the one the classify table names for the selected shape.
findings.observation: _captured_item_bytes writes Kind: <work_item.shape> and Detail: <partition> capture <capture_id>. The captured-item file grammar admits Kind values defect/design/research/intent only and requires Detail to be a repository-relative path matching the segment grammar, which admits no spaces. Kind: question — written for every routed question, one of the three work-item shapes — is outside the closed vocabulary, and the Detail value is prose, not a path.
findings.reachable_path: Every confirmed route: drain → transact_route → default_materialize writes docs/product/captured/<statement-slug>.md; question routes write Kind: question; all routes write the prose-formed Detail value. The files land in a directory whose generic readers validate the grammar without opt-in.
findings.rule_ref: docs/specs/work-item-promotion-handoff/spec.md § D2 — work-intake's classify table is the authority on what each shape produces — and Boundary — every destination is an existing owner with its own contract

findings.actual_failure: Reproduced: a drain closing one item with evidence returns a report whose closed entry holds only capture_id/action/ground — the evidence appears nowhere in the report — and the store disposition carries only rejected/closed_overtaken. A confirmed closure therefore leaves no evidence record anywhere in the repository, defeating § D5's closure accountability and leaving the § D12 rubric's closed-item criterion nothing to read.
findings.observation: decide_closure returns the operator-supplied closure evidence in its verdict, but drain's report entry for a closed item records only capture_id, action, and ground; the evidence is discarded, and no other surface in the delivery carries it.
findings.reachable_path: Every confirmed closure: drain → decide_closure (evidence in the returned verdict) → do_write (store event: disposition + ground-coded reason only) → items.append without the evidence.
findings.rule_ref: docs/specs/work-item-promotion-handoff/spec.md § D5 — the evidence rides the drain's run report, beside the closure it justifies — and Agent Rules / Always do

findings.actual_failure: _defect_ready treats that result as a completed, untruncated verification and proposes routing the defect, so a run whose evidence was cut short by the fallback-kill path can promote an item as verified — exactly the capped-run-must-hold outcome AC-0015 contracts, reached through the reader-join edge instead of the output cap itself.
findings.observation: After the wall-clock kill, run_stored_command joins the output-reader thread with reader.join(timeout=5.0) and never checks reader.is_alive(). On the kill-fallback path (killpg raised ProcessLookupError or PermissionError and a surviving grandchild still holds the pipe's write end), the join expires with the reader blocked mid-read and collected holding only a prefix of the output, yet the result reports outcome completed with output_truncated False.
findings.reachable_path: run_stored_command → timeout → killpg raises → process.kill() kills only the direct child → a grandchild keeps stdout's write end open → reader.join(5.0) expires with the thread alive → the function returns outcome completed, output_truncated False over a partial buffer.
findings.rule_ref: docs/specs/work-item-promotion-handoff/spec.md § D7 / AC-0015 — a run that does not complete within its caps is held rather than reported verified; _defect_ready's own docstring: a run terminated or truncated at a cap does not meet readiness
